subject: Evaluation MAP & Dedicated Reservation — pricing options and timeline
participants_external: sarah.li@arclight.ai (Sarah Li, Head of ML, Arclight Labs)
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@arclight.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@arclight.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:12:03 -0800
Subject: Exploring Dedicated eval + MAP for Q2

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the demo last week — the throughput numbers looked promising. Our team (ML + infra) wants to scope a short evaluation that maps to a mutual action plan (MAP) and a potential Dedicated reservation purchase. High-level asks:

- We want to run a 4‑week evaluation starting early March to validate perf at 2K concurrent tokens/sec workload (peaks).
- Need committed pool sizing guidance (GPUs / vGPU equivalents) and a pricing envelope for a 12‑month reserved term vs a 3‑month pilot.
- Would like explicit burst/overage rules (we can expect spikes during batch jobs).
- Procurement will want a simple acceptance milestone schedule tied to invoice triggers.

Can you send a proposed MAP that includes milestones (evaluation success criteria), a recommended GPU pool layout, and 1) pilot pricing and 2) 12‑month commit pricing with discount tiers? Also list what SOC2 evidence / audit artifacts you can surface for our compliance team.

I attached a short evaluation brief on our side (not included here).

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 30m call if that helps.

Best,
Sarah Li
Head of ML, Arclight Labs
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@arclight.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:03:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring Dedicated eval + MAP for Q2

Hi Sarah — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear asks. I put together a short MAP outline and a couple of pricing paths for pilot vs reserved 12‑month commitments. Attaching: Arclight_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP draft) and a placeholder quote (quote-reserved-capacity.pdf).

Quick notes in the meantime:
- Recommended pilot pool: 4 x A100‑80GB (or equivalent gst quantized variant) with autoscale to 6 for burst windows. This maps to your 2K tok/sec target based on our perf profile.
- Pilot pricing: monthly usage + $X/day for reserved baseline (see attached). Pilot term: 1 month (with optional 2 week rollback window).
- 12‑month reserved: two commit buckets we typically offer: 
  • Standard commit (12m): 30% discount vs on‑demand, includes defined COOP for burst up to +50% for limited windows with overage pricing at a predictable per‑token rate.
  • Growth commit (12m w/ ramp): lower initial commit with staged ramp (months 1–3) and higher discount (up to 40%) once ramp milestones are met.
- MAP milestones I propose: kickoff + infra access (week 0), baseline perf validation (end week 1), workload stress & KV cache validation (end week 2), acceptance run (end week 4). Each milestone has pass/fail criteria in the spreadsheet.

Can you confirm if the acceptance gate for invoicing should be on completion of the week‑4 acceptance run, or if procurement requires a separate signoff? I'll loop in Marissa and Priyom to fast follow on pricing and legal terms.

If useful, we can include CloudBridge (our marketplace partner) for procurement routing — James Evans does billing via marketplace in some regions.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:07:10 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Exploring Dedicated eval + MAP for Q2 — pricing help needed

Team — forwarding Sarah's ask and the MAP draft (attached). Key asks we need to price:
- 4‑week pilot (4 A100‑80GB equiv baseline, autoscale to 6 for bursts).
- 12‑month reserved options: (A) flat commit 4x baseline (steady) vs (B) ramp commit (start 2x months 1–3 then 8x by month 6).
- Define overage rates and a burst clause (we previously offered 50% burst allowance two times / month before overage billing).
- Discount tiers: 0–6 months pilot (no discount), 12m standard commit (30% off), 12m ramp commit (35–40% off after milestones).

Marissa — can you draft a short quote pdf and stripe/pricing lines we can share with Sarah + procurement? Priyom — any constraints on allowed burst clauses from infra/ops side (SRE concerns)? Monica — can you put together a short note on SOC2 artifact set we can provide?

Want to get back to Sarah by EOD tomorrow.

—Rafa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:21:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Exploring Dedicated eval + MAP for Q2 — pricing help needed

Rafael / team — see summary below (I'll produce quote-reserved-capacity.pdf from these lines).

Proposed pricing summary (topline):
- Pilot (4 x A100‑80GB equiv) — Monthly pilot fee: $26,000 + metered token usage at $0.0009/token for inference. Pilot includes up to 8 burst hours / month to 6 GPUs at no extra cost. Additional burst billed at $120/hr/GPU.

- 12‑month Reserved — Option A (Standard commit)
  • Commit: 4 GPUs continuously.
  • Effective discount: 30% vs on‑demand blended.
  • Burst: two free burst windows/month up to +50% capacity (capped 24 hours each) — overage billed at $0.07/token equivalent after cap.

- 12‑month Reserved — Option B (Growth ramp)
  • Commit schedule: Month1 2 GPUs, Month2 3 GPUs, Month3 4 GPUs, Month4+ target 8 GPUs.
  • Ramp milestones: perf validation at end week1 (month1), cache warmup at end week2 (month1), production acceptance at end month1.
  • Discount: starting 25% increasing to 40% once month4 target met.
  • Bursts: prioritized capacity allocation for ramp accounts; overage pricing at a discounted rate vs standard commit.

Notes / procurement guardrails:
- We recommend invoice trigger at completion of week‑4 acceptance run. Procurement sometimes prefers split invoicing: 30% on signature, 50% at acceptance, 20% on 30 day support handover — we can accommodate.
- We will include explicit SLAs for latency p95 during acceptance window; longer term SLA included in dedicated contracts.

Priyom — the burst clause above is what we typically offer. Do you want ops to confirm the 24h cap and free bursts frequency?

I'll have the formal quote created and share with Rafa.

-Marissa
VP, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@arclight.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@arclight.ai, James Evans <james.evans@cloudbridge.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:04:08 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation MAP & Dedicated Reservation — pricing options and timeline

Thanks Rafael and team — this is very helpful. A couple of follow ups before procurement finalizes paperwork: 

1) Acceptance milestone: procurement prefers split invoicing (30% on signature, 50% on acceptance after week‑4, 20% on 30 day handover). That aligns with Marissa's note — please reflect in the quote.
2) Burst clause: we need a hard SLA on burst availability for scheduled batch runs (we can give windows 72 hours in advance). Can Redwood guarantee prioritized capacity for those scheduled windows as part of the ramp commit? If so, include guarantee and the overage rate.
3) SOC2: can you share SOC2 scope doc and a short checklist of audit artifacts (logs, retention policies, key access matrix)? Monica — looping you for that.

If we can get a cleaned quote with the requested invoicing and a brief MAP timeline (matching milestones in Arclight_MAP_v1.xlsx) by EOD Tuesday our procurement team will start the PO. We can also route payment via CloudBridge marketplace if that simplifies billing — James, can you confirm marketplace billing path and any fees?

Happy to take a short call Tuesday 10am PT.

Best,
Sarah
Head of ML, Arclight Labs
